name: Shelter_Habitat
description: Player-built shelters for protection from weather and hostile environments.

questions.question: Does shelter-building teach real survival science?
questions.answer: Yes. Different materials have different insulation, structural integrity, and weather resistance. Player learns real material science.

questions.question: Does the player learn about material properties by choosing shelter materials?
questions.answer: Yes. Choosing between regolith brick, ice, metal, or composite teaches thermal and structural properties.

questions.question: Does shelter placement teach geography and microclimate awareness?
questions.answer: Yes. Sheltering in a canyon vs open plain vs crater affects wind exposure, temperature, and visibility.

questions.question: Can the player experiment with different shelter designs?
questions.answer: Yes. Players can build dome, underground, cliff-side, or modular structures with different tradeoffs.

questions.question: Is base-building a feature that drives Steam sales?
questions.answer: Yes. Base-building is one of the most wishlisted features in survival games.

questions.question: Does shelter construction generate shareable screenshots?
questions.answer: Yes. Player-built shelters in scenic locations generate social media shares.

questions.question: Does our shelter system differ from other survival games?
questions.answer: Our shelter system teaches real survival science. Other games use fictional mechanics.

questions.question: Is shelter-building satisfying and educational simultaneously?
questions.answer: Yes — building must be satisfying (snap-together modules, visual feedback) and educational simultaneously.

questions.question: Does weather physically affect shelter integrity?
questions.answer: Yes. Storms damage weak structures. Wind direction matters. Temperature affects internal climate.

questions.question: Do different biomes require different shelter strategies?
questions.answer: Yes. Ice caves need different shelter than desert mesas. Players must adapt.

questions.question: Can the player decorate and personalize their shelter?
questions.answer: Yes. Personalization drives emotional attachment to the base.

questions.question: Does the shelter interact with environment systems?
questions.answer: Yes. Solar panels need sun. Wind protection needs terrain. Thermal mass needs ground contact.

questions.question: Can shelter be implemented using existing procedural generation?
questions.answer: Basic shelter can use existing procedural generation (matter_gpu.py for terrain, spawn actor for modules).

questions.question: Does shelter require new UE5 systems?
questions.answer: Modular building can use UE5 actor spawning with snap-points. No destruction system needed for v1.

questions.question: Can a basic shelter be prototyped quickly?
questions.answer: Yes. A simple cube shelter with a door can be prototyped in a day using MCP actor spawning.

questions.question: Does shelter save/load work across sessions?
questions.answer: Yes. Shelter position, materials, and integrity can be saved to the save game system.

questions.question: Does the existing generator support modular actor spawning?
questions.answer: Partially. The generator creates actor classes. Modular spawning needs a new system.

questions.question: Is shelter data stored in the save game system?
questions.answer: Yes. Shelter state (position, materials, damage) can be serialized in the save game JSON.

questions.question: Can shelter placement be tested via sleepwalker?
questions.answer: Yes. Sleepwalker can verify shelter placement, weather interaction, and material properties.

questions.question: Does shelter need new MCP pathways?
questions.answer: Partially. Actor spawning works. Modular snap-building needs new MCP tools.

questions.question: Does this depend on weather system being complete?
questions.answer: Yes, depends on weather system being operational (otherwise shelter has no gameplay purpose).

questions.question: Does this depend on the generator for modular buildings?
questions.answer: Partially. Basic modules can be hand-placed. Generator support for modular buildings would be better.

questions.question: Does this prove survival mechanics work alongside education?
questions.answer: Yes. Proves survival mechanics work alongside educational systems, not against them.

questions.question: Was this derived from the original Loop 6 definition?
questions.answer: Derived from Loop 6 (Shelter) definition on the spiral board.

questions.question: Does shelter conflict with the educational scanner focus?
questions.answer: Minor resource conflict. Both need splat rendering but at different scales.

questions.question: What UE5 modular building knowledge is required?
questions.answer: UE5 modular building knowledge (actor spawning, snap-points, save/load).

questions.question: Does shelter-building serve the most famous educational RPG goal?
questions.answer: Yes. Teaching real survival science directly serves the educational RPG goal.

questions.question: What is sacrificed by building shelter systems now?

questions.question: What evidence shows base-building drives player retention?
questions.answer: Base-building has 2-3x higher player retention than non-base-building survival games.

questions.question: Does shelter chain reach a human learning real survival science?
questions.answer: Yes. Player learns real material science and survival principles through gameplay.

questions.question: How does shelter construction cost vs. quality create a housing economy where players balance material investment against survival needs and long-term maintenance costs?
questions.answer: Shelter is the largest capital investment. A basic shelter costs 50 units common material (easy to gather) but provides minimal insulation. A reinforced shelter costs 200 units including rare material but provides 3x durability. New players live cheaply but repair often; established players invest in premium shelters that reduce long-term maintenance. This is capital allocation: spend now on quality or later on repairs.

questions.question: Does building a shelter tell the story of making a home — from a bare survival pod to a personalized habitat with lights, furnishings, and the quiet evidence of a life being lived?
questions.answer: Every shelter tells a domestic story: the placement of furniture tells you how the player lives, the repairs tell you what the weather has done, the accumulated objects tell you how long they've stayed — a home with a biography.

questions.question: Can the player place and orient shelter modules using simple snap-points and grid alignment, without fighting the placement system or needing precise pixel-level cursor positioning?
questions.answer: Modules snap to a 1m grid with 45-degree rotation increments. Placement preview shows green (valid) / red (invalid) with collision highlight. Snap distance is generous (0.5m threshold). RMB rotates, LMB confirms. No precision aiming required.

questions.question: Does every shelter's structural state (module list, positions, connections, damage, resource inventory) need to persist?
questions.answer: Yes. Shelters have complex persistent state: list of placed modules with positions/rotations, module health/damage per module, stored resources, occupant count. This is heavy save data. Written on manual save or module change.

questions.question: What structural physics apply to shelters — load-bearing, stress distribution, collapse mechanics under weight or storm stress?
questions.answer: Simplified structural integrity model. Each module has a structural load capacity. Exceeding it (too many stacked modules, storm damage reducing capacity) causes progressive deformation then collapse. Collapse uses basic rigid body physics for debris.
